limitations: terminal control and aerodynamic families are explicit alternatives, never averaged
cruise fuel envelope is replaced by the explicit continuation condition using refined probability divided by old probability
fuel quantity and shared flow discrepancy are drawn jointly under the declared exhaustion interval
cruise Mach controls horizontal airspeed; the boundary retains its full horizontal and vertical velocity
terminal wind uses ERA5 plus the boundary wind residual held fixed during descent
pressure altitude is used as geometric height in this conditional point-mass approximation
these contact predictions do not condition on transmission availability or APU timing; power states remain recorded for separate hypotheses
BFO predictions are stored against the shared 00:11 bias state; sequence likelihood must update that bias jointly
unsupported terminal outcomes must be reported before conditioning any impact PDF
when a control proposal is enabled, its per-draw prior/proposal correction preserves the same physical control prior
impact angle is a velocity angle, not aircraft body pitch; acoustic coupling is not inferred here
